brief: Rates impact is starting to bite broader financial conditions (OAT-Bund and US high-yield spread widening), and central banks are pushing back, but their credibility depends on conditions staying tight or data softening. BofA holds its Fed call (75bp of hikes Sep-Dec 2026 to a 4.375% terminal rate), stays paid 2Y and in curve flatteners, and treats this week's data as the test: a below-consensus September payrolls print (BofA forecasts 60k vs 85k consensus) would bull-steepen the curve and pull terminal Fed pricing toward 4.55-4.6%, a stronger print would bear-flatten it toward 4.8%+. The recent 2s30s steepening reflects real-rate uncertainty and a vol spike, not a reversal of the hiking thesis. In Europe, the 10y OAT-Bund spread widened over 30bp to 140bp on technical and supply factors; BofA puts fair value at 100-110bp and lists five backstops against a move past 150bp. The RBA hiked to 4.60% but a downside CPI surprise pared back terminal pricing, so BofA stays paid November RBA OIS. In Japan, BofA frames long-end JGB yield gains as a global spillover rather than a domestic story and stays long 30-year JGBs on asset swap given resilient demand.
